quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: We're out of rice, oil, and salt.
quests.textToSpeak: We're out of rice, oil, and salt.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: Count the three items. Listen for whether the first two sound finished or as if something is still coming.
quests.explanation: The first two items lift slightly because more is coming, and only 'salt' falls to close the list. If each item fell, they would sound like three separate complaints.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Non-final items stay up; the last item brings the fall.

quests.instruction: You are reading a packing list aloud to a friend and haven't reached the end. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: Passport, phone charger,
quests.textToSpeak: Passport, phone charger,
options: Rise, rise, rise — list continues
Falling on last item — list complete
quests.hint: The line ends with a comma and no 'and'. Ask yourself whether the speaker has finished.
quests.explanation: The list is unfinished, so the pitch stays up after 'charger'. A fall would announce that you had nothing left to pack.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A rise on the last word spoken says: more to come.

quests.instruction: You tell a colleague what to bring on a rainy site visit. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: Bring a jacket, an umbrella, and boots.
quests.textToSpeak: Bring a jacket, an umbrella, and boots.
options: Fall on every item — separate statements
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.hint: You are naming three things in one breath. Decide which item should sound like the last.
quests.explanation: Keep 'jacket' and 'umbrella' slightly lifted, then fall on 'boots'. The fall tells your colleague the list is complete.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 In a spoken list, only the last item drops.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: I'll have the soup, a salad, and sparkling water.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll have the soup, a salad, and sparkling water.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: A customer is placing an order. Compare how 'soup' and 'water' end.
quests.explanation: The customer lifts through 'soup' and 'salad' to show the order continues, then falls on 'water'. The waiter knows it's safe to write it down.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A waiter listens for the fall to know the order is done.

quests.instruction: A receptionist explains what your hotel room includes and pauses mid-list. Which pattern fits her pause?
quests.word: The room has a desk, a fridge,
quests.textToSpeak: The room has a desk, a fridge,
options: Rise, rise, rise — list continues
Falling on last item — list complete
quests.hint: She stops after 'fridge' but you know she isn't finished. What in the voice tells you this?
quests.explanation: The pitch stays up after 'fridge', which signals that more amenities follow. A fall would mean the list ended after two items.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A held-up ending tells the listener to keep waiting.

quests.instruction: You're describing your day-off routine to a new colleague. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: I usually cook, clean, and call my parents.
quests.textToSpeak: I usually cook, clean, and call my parents.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: These are three short activities in a row. Think about which word sounds final.
quests.explanation: Lift lightly on 'cook' and 'clean', then fall on 'parents'. The fall gives a sense of a finished, natural routine.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Short verbs in a list are lifted, and the last phrase falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
options: Fall at the end of every single group
Rise on each group, fall on the last
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on each group, fall on the last
quests.hint: Phone numbers are read in small groups. Listen for what happens at the end of each group.
quests.explanation: Each group ends with a slight rise so the listener knows more digits are coming. The final group falls, signaling that the number is done.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Digit groups lift, and the last group falls to close the number.

quests.instruction: You're on the phone with a booking agent who is reading you a reference code. Which pattern fits the agent's voice?
quests.word: The code is K-T-4, 9-2, R-M.
quests.textToSpeak: The code is K-T-4, 9-2, R-M.
options: Level on each group, rise on the last group
Rise on each group, fall on the last
quests.correctAnswer: Rise on each group, fall on the last
quests.hint: Letters and numbers are given in chunks. Compare the group endings with the final group.
quests.explanation: Grouping helps memory, so each chunk lifts a little. The last chunk falls to show the code is over.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Chunks lift to say 'continue'; the last chunk falls to say 'stop'.

quests.instruction: You give your home address to a courier over the phone. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: It's 14 Harbour Road, Unit 6, Cape Town.
quests.textToSpeak: It's 14 Harbour Road, Unit 6, Cape Town.
options: Fall, fall, fall — three separate facts
Rise, rise, fall — address complete
quests.hint: An address has several parts. Decide which part closes it.
quests.explanation: 'Harbour Road' and 'Unit 6' lift because the address is still going. 'Cape Town' falls to finish it. The courier hears each part as belonging to one address.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Parts of an address lift until the final place name.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: The flat has two bedrooms, a small balcony, a shared garden, and a parking space.
quests.textToSpeak: The flat has two bedrooms, a small balcony, a shared garden, and a parking space.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: Four items are named. Notice whether the speaker sounds like they've finished after the third one.
quests.explanation: In longer lists, each item keeps a small lift so the listener expects more. The fall comes only on 'space', which ends the description.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Longer lists need a steady lift all the way to the last item.

quests.instruction: A friend is describing a new job while you wait for the last benefit. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: They offer health insurance, extra holidays, a gym pass,
quests.textToSpeak: They offer health insurance, extra holidays, a gym pass,
options: Rise, rise, rise — list continues
Falling on last item — list complete
quests.hint: The list is unfinished, and you can hear it. Which item sounds like it isn't the last?
quests.explanation: The speaker keeps the pitch up after 'pass' because a fourth benefit is coming. A fall would sound like the whole list had ended.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ Hold the pitch on the last item you say if you're not done.

quests.instruction: You list what you learned on a training course. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: I learned about budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and team planning.
quests.textToSpeak: I learned about budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and team planning.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: Four topics in a row. Decide which of them should end the sequence.
quests.explanation: Lift each of the first three topics, then fall on 'planning'. The steady lifts keep the listener expecting more, and the final fall closes it.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 With four items, keep the small lifts even and drop on the last.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: They sell notebooks, pens, folders, that sort of thing.
quests.textToSpeak: They sell notebooks, pens, folders, that sort of thing.
options: Falling on last item — list complete
Rising on last item — list left open
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on last item — list left open
quests.hint: The speaker ends with a general phrase, not a final item. Listen for how open the ending sounds.
quests.explanation: 'That sort of thing' means the list isn't exhaustive, so the pitch stays up and open. A firm fall would sound as if these four were the only items.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A left-open list keeps a lifted ending.

quests.instruction: A manager lists what a project needs and leaves it open. Which pattern fits her last words?
quests.word: We'll need budgets, timelines, resources, and so on.
quests.textToSpeak: We'll need budgets, timelines, resources, and so on.
options: Rising on last item — list left open
Falling on last item — list complete
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on last item — list left open
quests.hint: 'And so on' suggests there are more items not mentioned. Consider how the voice sounds when it is unfinished.
quests.explanation: The final phrase invites the listener to imagine other things, so the pitch stays up. It's a way of saying 'you know what I mean'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ 'And so on' calls for a lifted or level ending.

quests.instruction: You're telling a friend about weekend plans that are not fixed. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: We might go hiking, visit the market, see a film, whatever.
quests.textToSpeak: We might go hiking, visit the market, see a film, whatever.
options: Rising on last item — list left open
Falling on last item — list complete
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on last item — list left open
quests.hint: 'Whatever' shows the plans are loose. Decide whether your voice should sound decided.
quests.explanation: With loose plans, the pitch doesn't close on 'whatever'. It stays level or slightly up, which shows you're flexible.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ Relaxed, open plans rarely end with a hard fall.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: Today I'll finish the report, reply to emails, and prepare for the call.
quests.textToSpeak: Today I'll finish the report, reply to emails, and prepare for the call.
options: Fall on every item — separate statements
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.hint: These are three tasks in a plan. Ask which one closes the list.
quests.explanation: Each task before the last lifts so the plan keeps going. 'Call' falls, giving a confident sense of closure.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 A work plan sounds organized when only the last task falls.

quests.instruction: Your teammate is reviewing what remains. She hasn't finished. Which pattern fits her pause?
quests.word: Still to do: the slides, the handout,
quests.textToSpeak: Still to do: the slides, the handout,
options: Falling on last item — list complete
Rise, rise, rise — list continues
quests.hint: She lists items and stops mid-thought. What does the raised ending tell you?
quests.explanation: The lifted ending on 'handout' suggests she has more to add. A fall would be understood as 'nothing else'.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ Mid-list pauses keep the pitch up.

quests.instruction: You explain what the customer complained about. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: They complained about the delay, the noise, and the price.
quests.textToSpeak: They complained about the delay, the noise, and the price.
options: Fall on every item — separate statements
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.hint: Three separate complaints appear in one sentence. Decide which word should fall.
quests.explanation: Lift on 'delay' and 'noise' to show more complaints follow. Fall on 'price' to show that was the last.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Grouped complaints sound like one report when only the last falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: Could you bring plates, glasses, and napkins?
quests.textToSpeak: Could you bring plates, glasses, and napkins?
options: Rise, rise, rise — request ends open
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.correctAnswer: Rise, rise, rise — request ends open
quests.hint: This is a request, not a plain statement. Compare the ending with a normal list.
quests.explanation: Because this is a yes/no request, the final item also rises. The listener answers yes or no. A falling last item would sound like an order.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 In a list-question, the last item rises because the sentence is a question.

quests.instruction: A friend is asking what they should buy for the party. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: Do we need chips, drinks, or dessert?
quests.textToSpeak: Do we need chips, drinks, or dessert?
options: Rise, rise, rise — open question
Rise, rise, fall — choose among items
quests.correctAnswer: Rise, rise, fall — choose among items
quests.hint: 'Or' offers items to choose from. Think about whether the friend wants to hear about all of them.
quests.explanation: With 'or' and a set of options, the pitch falls on the last item. The friend picks from what they hear.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 An 'or' list in a question ends with a fall.

quests.instruction: You want to know if your neighbor has any of these tools. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: Do you have a hammer, nails, or a screwdriver?
quests.textToSpeak: Do you have a hammer, nails, or a screwdriver?
options: Rise, rise, fall — choose one
Rise, rise, rise — any of these?
quests.correctAnswer: Rise, rise, rise — any of these?
quests.hint: You are hoping for a yes to any of them. Decide whether you're asking about a single choice.
quests.explanation: You are asking whether the neighbor has any of the tools, not to pick one, so the last item also rises.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 If any answer is welcome, every item keeps the lift.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: First open the app, then tap Settings, and finally choose Language.
quests.textToSpeak: First open the app, then tap Settings, and finally choose Language.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: These are steps in a process. Notice how the speaker signals that 'Language' is the last step.
quests.explanation: Sequence words like 'then' keep steps linked. The lift on earlier steps and the fall on 'Language' show the process is done.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 In instructions, steps lift; the last step falls.

quests.instruction: A friend is guiding you through a recipe over the phone and pauses. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: Chop the onions, add the garlic,
quests.textToSpeak: Chop the onions, add the garlic,
options: Falling on last item — list complete
Rise, rise, rise — list continues
quests.hint: The speaker is mid-instruction. Listen to whether it feels like the end.
quests.explanation: The pitch stays up after 'garlic', so you know there is another step. A fall would suggest you should start cooking.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ Mid-instruction pauses lift so the listener waits.

quests.instruction: You explain how to reach your office to a visitor. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: Turn left at the bank, walk past the cafe, and we're on the right.
quests.textToSpeak: Turn left at the bank, walk past the cafe, and we're on the right.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: There are three parts to these directions. Decide which part should sound final.
quests.explanation: Lift on 'bank' and 'cafe' to keep the directions connected, then fall on 'right'. The visitor knows they've heard everything.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Directions chain together with lifts and close with one fall.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: It's cheap, it's close, and it's quiet.
quests.textToSpeak: It's cheap, it's close, and it's quiet.
options: Fall on every item — separate statements
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.hint: Three short reasons for choosing an apartment. Listen for the point where the argument closes.
quests.explanation: Each reason lifts to build the case, and the fall on 'quiet' closes the argument. The listener hears one persuasive list.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Reasons build with lifts and land on a fall.

quests.instruction: Your friend is convincing you to join a gym and hasn't finished. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: It's affordable, it's open late,
quests.textToSpeak: It's affordable, it's open late,
options: Falling on last item — list complete
Rise, rise, rise — list continues
quests.hint: This is an argument in progress. Ask yourself whether more points are coming.
quests.explanation: The pitch stays up after 'late' because another reason is coming. A fall would end the argument.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️ A persuasive list keeps the pitch up until the final point.

quests.instruction: You're asked to describe your last manager. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: She was organized, patient, and always fair.
quests.textToSpeak: She was organized, patient, and always fair.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Fall on every item — separate statements
quests.hint: The adjectives are compliments in a row. Decide which adjective completes the description.
quests.explanation: Lift on 'organized' and 'patient' to keep praising, then fall on 'fair'. The fall gives the last compliment weight.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 The last adjective gets the fall and the strongest impact.

quests.instruction: Identify the intonation
quests.word: I bought apples, bananas, oranges, and some grapes.
quests.textToSpeak: I bought apples, bananas, oranges, and some grapes.
options: Fall on every item — separate statements
Rise, rise, fall — list complete
quests.hint: Four fruits are named. Notice which one sounds like the last.
quests.explanation: Each fruit lifts slightly, and the last one falls. The steady rising steps keep the listener following the list.
quests.pitchRule: ↗️📉 Lifts through the list, then one fall at the end.

quests.instruction: A doctor is asking about symptoms and leaves the list open. Which pattern fits?
quests.word: Any fever, cough, headache, anything like that?
quests.textToSpeak: Any fever, cough, headache, anything like that?
options: Falling on the last phrase — closed list
Rising on the last phrase — open question
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on the last phrase — open question
quests.hint: The doctor wants a yes to any symptom. Decide whether the list is closed.
quests.explanation: 'Anything like that' keeps the question open, so the pitch rises to the end. The doctor wants to hear about any symptom.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 An open-ended list-question ends with a rise.

quests.instruction: You are ending a long email summary out loud. Which pattern will you use?
quests.word: So that covers pricing, timing, and next steps.
quests.textToSpeak: So that covers pricing, timing, and next steps.
options: Rise, rise, fall — list complete
Rising on last item — list left open
quests.hint: You're wrapping up. Decide whether you want to sound finished or leave the door open.
quests.explanation: 'Next steps' falls to show the summary is complete. A rise would invite more topics, which you don't want here.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 A summary closes with a firm fall on the last item.
